problem: A pet center registered $34$ dogs and $29$ cats on a particular day. Of the dogs registered that day, $12$ were vaccinated. Of the cats registered that day, $15$ were vaccinated. What is the probability that a randomly selected pet registered that day was vaccinated?

feedback.problem: A company manufactures electronic components. The components are produced by two machines, $A$ and $B.$ In a particular random sample, $37$ of the components sampled were produced by machine $A,$ and $43$ were produced by machine $B.$ On inspecting the sampled components, it was found that $5$ defective components were produced by machine $A$ and $3$ defective components were produced by machine $B.$ What is the probability that a randomly selected component from the sample is defective?
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the event that the chosen component was produced by machine $A$, and let $D$ be the event that the chosen component is defective. Then ${A}^{′}$ is the event that the component was produced by machine $B.$

To calculate the probability that the randomly selected component is defective, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
P(D)=P(D\cap A)+P(D\cap {A}^{′})
$$

To calculate $P(D\cap A),$ we take the number of defective components produced by machine $A,$ and divide by the total number of defective components $(37+43=80).$ So, we have

$$
P(D\cap A)=\frac{5}{80}.
$$

Similarly, to calculate $P(D\cap {A}^{′}),$ we take the number of defective components produced by machine $B,$ and divide by the total number of defective components $(37+43=80).$ So, we have

$$
P(D\cap {A}^{′})=\frac{3}{80}.
$$

Finally, substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected component is defective is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D) & =P(D\cap A)+P(D\cap {A}^{′}) \\  & =\frac{5}{80}+\frac{3}{80} \\  & =\frac{8}{80} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
